content.text: Conditions or Triggers are used in scripting to restrict events and commands to correct targets.

items.text: In condition blocks ( trigger section of events , or equivalent: mult_modifier , can_use_title , potential , allow , ...)
In the limit clause of command blocks
In scripted triggers , which can be used to group conditions into re-usable macro.
At the root of events for pre-triggers used to improve performances

content.text:
Syntax for most conditions accepting numeric values was extended with numeric operators since version 2.8.
The following triggers do not (fully) support these operators:

items.text: tier (as well as similar triggers, such as (lower/higher_)(real_)tier(_than)
heavy_troops , light_troops (simple right-hand side only, clause form fully support numeric operators)

content.text: Available conditions depend on the current scope type.

rows: Checks adventurer flag of the title (title that gets destroyed whenever the holder gains another title or when the holder dies).
Checks the age of a character, in whole years, rounded down.
Checks the absolute value of the age difference in years between two characters, rounded down. Typically used in conjunction with is_older_than .
Checks if the character is a player or an AI.
Check an AI behavior modifier (based on traits )
Check an AI behavior modifier (based on traits )
Check an AI behavior modifier (based on traits )
Check an AI behavior modifier (based on traits )
Check an AI behavior modifier (based on traits )

Can be used to fail a trigger clause, without needing to comment/delete the code ( always = no ). Also used to test if (enough, using count ) scopes do or do not exist, or if a suitable event target could be found and saved, using a random_ scope, evaluating to false if no matching scope is found.

NOT = { any_ward = { always = yes } }
event_target:test = { always = yes }

Checks if the character is among the nth most powerful vassals of the realm. It compares the character's powerbase with that of all other direct vassals of the same liege. Also see is_powerful_vassal and relative_power . Does not permit the use of 2.8+ comparison operators!
Checks if any religion has been generated within the specified distance. Only used in alternate start generation.
(2.8) Checks to see if the scoped artifact is the same as the target artifact.
(2.8) Checks to see if the artifact is older than the specified value. Always returns false if the artifact has no known creation date.
(2.8) Checks if the scoped artifact can be gifted to the target character.
Checks if the scoped artifact is of the given type
Checks if the given character owns at least one instance of the scoped artifact.
Checks the difference in specified attribute with the target character. Can use negative values to see if the current scope is worse.
Checks if two characters are in the same location. If target is a title, uses the current location of the titleholder.
Checks for hidden attribute base health
Checks if the scoped bloodline is the exact same bloodline as the target bloodline. Note that this compares bloodlines, not bloodline types.
Checks if the scoped bloodline is active for the target character.
Checks if the trovince borders a lake
Checks if the province borders a major river
Checks if the specified amount of the triggers contained inside are met. [1]

In this example at least 3 of the 5 triggers need to return true: calc_true_if = {
    amount >= 3
    culture = swedish
    religion = catholic
    is_female = no
    is_adult = yes
    age >= 50
}
Checks if the title is not occupied, has no holdings being sieged, or contested in war and is not the holder's capital. Also see num_of_extra_landed_titles .
Checks if character is not a religious head or leader of a holy order.
Checks if character is the head of a religion that uses crusades. If the religion uses the new-style crusade, also checks if no other religion is currently organising/fighting such a crusade.
Checks if the target character has at least one personality trait that the scoped character does not have
Checks if scoped ruler can grant at least one target minor title
Checks if it is possible to travel by land between two provinces. Can be expanded to also take a distance parameter.
Checks if it is possible to travel by sea between two provinces. Both provinces have to be sea or coastal. Can be expanded to also take a distance parameter.
Checks if character has fewer than the maximum of leadership traits, as set in defines.
Checks the conditions for the specified councillor position or minor title.
Checks if scope character can join the specified society.

Checks if the character is old enough to marry (see is_marriage_adult has no traits with cannot_marry = yes , is not a priest of a religion that prohibits priest marriage, is not a member of a holy order and is not already betrothed or married, even if their religion allows polygamy. If the right-hand side is a character, checks the previous for both characters, and if characters are of opposite sex.
Checks if the character scope you're currently in can see the target character's secret religion.
Checks if a character can get the job position of the target character and vice versa.

Checks if the specified casus belli would show up and be usable in the UI. By default, everything in the CB is checked, including all of the extra hardcoded restrictions applicable to all war declarations (eg. no raised levies, not bankrupt, not already at war with defender, not in a NAP with defender, no hostages). Parameter Type Description target character/title Required. What character or title to target. casus_belli CB Required. What CB to use. thirdparty_title title Optional. What title to target, if relevant. thirdparty character Optional. What character to declare war on the behalf of, if relevant. only_check_triggers boolean Optional. Defaults to "no". If "yes", seems to only check the can_use block of the CB definition. If "no", seems to check everything ( can_use , can_use_gui , can_use_title , hardcoded restrictions, CB flags like allowed_to_target_tributaries = no ). Note: Not every possible CB property has been tested, use with care and verify for yourself! For technical reasons, thirdparty claimant wars require the current scope to be the claimant and thirdparty the attacker. All other CBs work intuitively, using above syntax.
Checks if two characters are the same.
Checks if a variable satisfies the comparison.
Checks if the target character has any kind of claim on the scoped title.
Checks if the character is the head of a nomadic clan, or title is a nomadic clan.
Checks if the scope's clan opinion of who is at least this value
Checks if the scoped character's clan opinion difference of the first and second target characters satisfies the value comparison.
Checks a character's personal combat skill against a fixed integer value

Checks if a province has a winter climate defined in /map/climate.txt - does NOT check whether province is currently experiencing a winter, use is_winter for that. Note that you can only check for winter types ( mild_winter , normal_winter , severe_winter ), and not for temperate climate; but obviously any province that does not have a winter climate is temperate.
Checks combat rating (personal combat skill) difference with another character
Checks the number of traits with inherit_chance greater than 0.

Checks if the scoped character controls (personally or via a vassal) all the baronies under specified title. Notes: the title itself doesn't need to exist. completely_controls is true if title name is invalid.
Checks if the title flag conquest_culture is set to a certain culture. Certain CBs set conquest_culture (used for cultural conversion events, and faction membership).
Supplanted by more flexible region trigger, but still works
Checks if province/holding is occupied (war) by another character/realm, or if the holding/province is not sieged down and held by target character
Checks if scoped character has province in own demesne and is unsieged, or has sieged down this province. Only takes province ID, so of very limited use.

Checks if the character isthe head of their religion (holder of a title with a flag controls_religion = <religion> ). Does not include antipopes, pentarchs and autocephalous patriachs - see rightful_religious_head .

(2.8) Checks if the scoped character is young enough to be the target character's parent. This means that they're at least AGE_OF_MARRIAGE_MALE years younger, and at most MAX_CHILD_BIRTH_AGE years younger if the target is female (for immortal characters, as long as they became immortal before this age they bypass the check). It also checks if they didn't die before the birth date of the scoped character.

(2.8) Checks if the scoped character is old enough to be the target character's parent. This means that they're at least AGE_OF_MARRIAGE_MALE years older, and at most MAX_CHILD_BIRTH_AGE years older if female (for immortal characters, as long as they became immortal before this age they bypass the check). It also checks if they didn't die before the birth date of the target.
Checks number of elements matched by a scope and some limit . Since patch 2.3 works with all any_ scopes. Does not work in traits with cached = yes associated scopes.
Checks the artifact pot for the on-going new-style Crusade
Checks the gold pot for the on-going new-style Crusade
Checks the piety pot for the on-going new-style Crusade
Checks the gold pot for the on-going new-style Crusade
Checks the military strength of the defenders to the military strength of the preparing attackers in a new-style Crusade. Doesn't work.
Checks the military strength of the preparing attackers to the military strength of the defenders in a new-style Crusade
Checks how many days have passed since the preparation of the current new-style Crusade started
Checks how many days remain before the current new-style Crusade will start in earnest
Checks if the character has this specific culture
Checks if the character is part of the target scope's culture group
Checks the day of a character's a date of birth.
Checks if scope character has been at current rank in society for the given number of days.
Checks if scope character has been in a society for the given number of days
Checks how long ago a character participated in a war, either through combat or siege. Does not support numeric operators.
Checks how many days have passed since the last policy change of the scoped offmap power.
Checks how many days have passed since the last status change of the scoped offmap power.
Checks if scoped character is defending in a war with any claim CB for specified title against specified character
Checks if demesne limit divided by current demesne size is higher than specified value. Does not support numeric operators.
Checks if the garrison of all demesne holdings satisfies the specified amount
Checks if the character has a minimum of this demesne size
(2.8) Checks if the current demesne size divided by the demesne limit satisfies the specified comparison.

Checks if the current scope is a de facto vassal of the target scope, even if not de jure. Can check, for example, if a barony is not held under its de jure liege title, without checking liege relationship of the title's holders.
Checks if the current scope is a de facto vassal of the right hand side scope.
Checks if the current scope is a direct de jure vassal of right hand side scope.
Checks if the current scope is a de jure vassal of right hand side scope.
Checks if current scope is a de jure liege of right hand side scope.
Checks the death reason of a dead character
Checks if the province has the specified disease.
Checks if the province has at least the specified disease defence modifier.

Checks if the scoped character matches the current dislike of the offmap power of the specified type .  If the dislike trigger has a context, the context parameter must match to return true. If the dislike trigger has no context, the context parameter must be omitted to return true.
Checks the game's difficulty setting. Valid values: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 very_easy, easy, normal, hard, very_hard
Checks a character's personal diplomacy attribute against another character or a fixed integer value. Also see realm_diplomacy .
Checks if character has the diplomatic_immunity flag, protecting him from hostile actions.

Checks if the distance between the provinces corresponding to the current and target scopes satisfies the specified value. Distances are pixels within the main map images and positions.txt. Calculates distances between provinces, not characters. If the current or target scope is a character, their capital scope is used, not their current location. If a target title is provided, it uses the title's holder's capital scope. To calculate distance between characters, use location = {} on both characters.

Checks if the smallest distance between two character's realms (the distance between the two provinces closest in proximity to each other) or the smallest distance between a province and a character's realm satisfies the specified comparison. Always compares between the top liege's realms of both parties involved. If a title is provided, it uses the title's holder.
Checks if the character's dynastic prestige satisfies the specified comparison.
Checks the character's dynasty, indexed by an integer value. Lowborn characters (no dynasty) match none or no value.
Checks the combined troop strength of all vassals of the same dynasty of the scoped character compared to that character's liege's troop strength.
Checks if the character has the Excommunicated trait and is of the same religion of the target character.

Checks if a faction exists in the realm of the currently scoped character. [2] Parameter Description faction Required title Optional, only needed if the faction has a target title thirdparty Optional, only needed if the faction has a third party, such as claimant factions
Checks if a faction has the specified amount of power. Used in vassal scope who is in the faction.
Checks if a pregnant woman's unborn child has a known father.
Checks the character's fertility value. In-game, can only be seen through the charinfo console command.
Checks if a combat flank has a leader. Used in combat tactics.
Checks if a combat flank is using a specific tactic.
Checks if a fort has at least one building.
Checks if a fort has the specified building.
Checks if a fort is currently constructing the specified building.
Checks how many free court slots a ruler has
Checks if the scoped character is of the same dynasty as its liege.

Check government type of a character. For checking government groups, see is_feudal , is_republic , etc. Provinces must be by relative scope or saved event target, since numbers are interpreted as character IDs.

government = nomadic_government
government = k_norway
government = ROOT

Checks a character's graphical culture. This is different from the effect set_graphical_culture which takes a culture, not a culturegfx. In-game, can only be seen through the "charinfo" console command. Fixed in 2.8. (In 2.7 and earlier, checking against an invalid culturegfx will cause a CTD.)

Checks if if the scope has had that flag for the specified amount of time. Works for any scope that can store flags, unlike the more specific had_ scope _flag triggers. Before 3.0 months and years do not work as parameters, only days does. Note: Does not work on bloodline scope! Parameter Type Description flag flag Required, flag to be checked years/months/days int Required, time since the flag should have been set
Offmap-specific version of had_flag . Does not appear to be functioning as of at least version 3.3.0 - use had_flag instead.
Offmap-specific version of had_flag . Excludes flags defined in the offmap status or policy files.
Checks specified settings/parameters used in alternate world generation.
Checks if a character has a/no/specific ambition.
Checks if the holding has any building has_any_building = no does not work, use NOT = { has_any_building = yes } instead.
Checks if the scoped character has the specified opinion modifier to any other character..
Checks if the scoped character has a quest.
Checks if scoped character has any traits with is_symptom = yes . has_any_symptom = no does not work, use NOT = { has_any_symptom = yes } instead.
Checks if the scoped character owns an artifact by that name.
Checks to see if the character has assigned a particular minor title, optionally with a specified amount.
Checksd if scoped character has a blood oath with target character
Checks if a holding has the specified building (buildings under construction do not count).
Checks if scope's religion has an ongoing crusade war.
Checks if scoped province has a capital holding.
Checks if a province has a castle holding.
Checks if scoped character can use any CB against target character.
Checks if a character has the specified modifier
Checks if a character has children, dead or alive. Functionally identical to num_of_children >= 1 .
Checks if a province has a city holding.
Checks if a character has any type of claim on target title.
Checks if scoped character has an army engaged in combat in the target province. Only takes province IDs, generates no tooltips.
Checks if a character's council can vote on anything. See enable_council_voting_on_issue and disable_council_voting_on_issue .
Used in conjunction with set_councilor_faction_join_restriction . Doesn't do anything by itself.
If king or empire tier, checks if title has a holder, otherwise checks if any de jure liege title is king or empire tier and has a holder.
Checks if the scope's religion has an ongoing new-style Crusade. Also see is_preparing_crusade .
Checks if the wonder has a description set by history
Checks if the wonder has a name set by the player or by history
Checks if target character holds any de jure liege title of scoped title.
Checks if province is currently experiencing an outbreak of any disease.

Checks if the user has a specified DLC. Values: "The Sword of Islam", "Legacy of Rome", "Sunset Invasion", "The Republic", "The Old Gods", "Sons of Abraham", "Rajas of India", "Charlemagne", "Way of Life", "Horse Lords", "Zeus" and "Conclave" (both are equivalent), "Reapers", "Mystics", "Jade Dragon", "Holy Fury".
Checks if a character's dynasty has the specified modifier
Checks if the character owns any event spawned army given an earmark with the spawn_unit command.
Checks if the character owns any event spawned army, not currently raiding, given an earmark with the spawn_unit command.
Checks elector stance for a title's election.
Checks if the scoped character is currently embargoing the target character.
Checks if the province has an empty holding slot. A holding under construction does not count.
Checks if the character has a trait with is_epidemic = yes , or if the province has an epidemic disease.
Checks if the scoped character is in a nomadic feud with target character.

Checks if the current scope has a given flag. Works for any scope that can store flags, unlike the more specific has_ scope _flag triggers. Note: "flags" in CKII scripting are not pre-determined or stored anywhere, they are dynamically created in the script. A mistyped flag will not be caught by the Validator, as there are no "invalid" flags. Also see flags . Note: Does not work on bloodline scope!
Checks if a character has a/no/specific focuses .
Checks if the province has a fort
Checks if the character has no free court slots left
Checks if a game rule is active. See game rules modding .
Checks if the game is in the pre-game character selection screen.
Checks if the character has a guardian assigned.
Checks if the offmap power has had the target name localisation key in the past.
Checks if the scope's religion has heresies.
Checks if the province has any technology advance over the target character's capital province or target province.
Checks if a title is currently held by a character.
Checks if the province has a hospital.
Checks if the holding has the given holding modifier
Check if the culture has the horde = yes flag defined.
Checks if the character in the current scope has a trait with the flag cannot_inherit = yes .
Checks if the character has amount of times the given character modifier
Checks if the holding has a amount of times the given holding modifier
Checks if the province has a amount of times the given province modifier
Checks if the character is currently carrying out the target job action.
Checks if the character has the target council position. With "yes", checks whether the character has any council position (not including Advisor).
(2.8) Checks if the artifact has a creation date on record.
Checks if the scoped character holds the target title. Note that its holder may be unlanded (not holding any barony/county titles), if the title is of the landless type.
Checks if a title, or a ruler's primary title, or a courtier's liege's primary title has the target law.
Checks if the character's liege is currently enforcing realm peace. Also see will_liege_enforce_peace .
Checks if the character has living children.
Checks if the character has a lover
Checks if character has already created a mercenary band.
Checks for a static modifier added via set_mercenary_maintenance_modifier on scoped mercenary tile.
Checks if the character has a specific minor title or religious title, or any at all.
Checks if the character at least as much wealth as their liege
Checks if scoped character has a fleet in the target sea province. Only takes province IDs, generates no tooltips.
Checks if a character received a title recently enough that the penalties for being over the demesne limit is not yet active.
Can be used to check for a specific nickname, or (not) having any nickname.
Checks if a character a non-aggression pact with another character.
Checks a character's currency in the specified offmap ID.
Offmap-specific version of has_flag . Includes flags set by default in its current status or policy, by use of the flags = { } array.
Checks if the scoped offmap power has the specified localisation key as its current name.
Checks if the player ruler has chosen to receive news events from the specified offmap power through the interface.
Offmap-specific version of has_flag . Excludes flags defined in the offmap status or policy files.
Checks if the scoped character has the given opinion modifier towards who character
Checks if the character controls holdings not reachable across land from the capital.
Checks if the province has an owner. Useful to filter wasteland provinces.
Checks if the scope's religion has the pentarchy = yes flag.
Checks if a character has pledged defense for the new-style Crusade being planned
Checks if a character has pledged participation for the new-style Crusade being planned
Checks if the character has any/no or a specific plot.
Checks if the scoped offmap power currently has the specified offmap policy (defined in /common/offmap_powers/policies).
Checks if the scoped offmap power's current policy has the specified flag (defined in /common/offmap_powers/policies).
Checks if a character has a given portrait property/overlay/etc.
Checks if the the voting attitude of a councillor matches the target attitude or that of the target character. Also see is_voter . Not to be confused with has_minor_title or has_job_title .
Checks if the character has a weak or strong pressed (inheritable) claim on the target title.
Checks if the province has the given province modifier
Checks if the scoped character has the target quest.
Checks if the scoped ruler has raised levies of the target ruler.
Checks if a holy order or mercenary band has raised troops, testing if they are currently being hired by anyone.
Checks if the character is in a regency, for any reason.
Checks if the character has any raised levies, event troops or holy orders/mercenary bands.
Checks if character religion has a specific feature
Checks if the scope's religion has any religion features
Checks if the character secretly follows another religion
Checks if the target religion feature has been selected in the reformation screen
Checks if a holding is under construction in the province
Checks if the holding is under siege.
Checks if character has enough unused retinue cap for target retinue type
Checks if a province/character has started  building a tier/stage of a wonder. Can check particular wonders as well. Is not affected by pausing
Checks if a wonder has started constructing an upgrade. Can check particular wonder upgrades as well. Is not affected by pausing
Checks if the scoped offmap power currently has the specified offmap status modifier (defined in /common/offmap_powers/statuses).
Checks if the scoped offmap power has the specified flag in its current offmap status modifier's flags list.
Checks if the character has a strong claim, pressed or unpressed, on the target title.

Checks if the character has a strong pressed (inheritable) claim on the target title. Note: Broken in 3.3.5.1: has_strong_pressed_claim = SCOPE functions the same as has_weak_claim = SCOPE . NOT = { has_strong_pressed_claim = SCOPE } functions the same as NOT = { has_weak_pressed_claim = SCOPE } . Tooltips are the same as for has_weak_pressed_claim in both cases.
Checks if a province has a temple holding
Checks if the character has a traits with terrain command modifier for terrain matching the target terrain, or any trait with a command modifier for terrain.
Checks if the province has a trade post
Checks if a province has a tribal holding
Checks if scoped character has a truce with target character. Note that truces are one-way.
Checks if scoped character has an army in the target land or sea province. Only takes province IDs, generates no tooltips.
Checks if the character has any weak claim, pressed or unpressed, on the target title.
Checks if the character has a weak pressed (ininheritable) claim on the target title.

Checks if the scoped character is the current owner of any wonders, or if the scoped province contains any wonders. Can check particular wonders as well. Only applies for wonders that have completed first stage.
Checks if a wonder upgrade has a particular upgrade, or if it has any whatsoever.
Checks a character's health value. In-game, can only be seen through the "charinfo" console command.
Checks the number of traits with is_health = yes

Checks if scoped character held a favor activated on target character. The reverse condition is owed_favor_activated_on . Province scopes must be relative or saved event targets, since numbers are interpreted as character IDs.

Checks if all of a character's personally held titles' values sum up to the specified comparison, either another character, or a fixed value. 100 points per held barony title, 300 per held county/duchy title, 400 per kingdom and 500 per empire title.
Same as higher_tier_than but ignores temporary titles
Check that the tier of scoped character/title is strictly higher than the given tier.
Checks if character is historical (either by being scripted in character history, or created as historical by script), or part of an ongoing event chain
Checks if title is held by target character
Checks if the holding is of the target type city / temple / castle / tribal / nomad / family_palace
Checks how full the holding's garrison is. 1 is 100%, 0 is 0%.
Checks how full the holding's raisable levy is. 1 is 100%, 0 is 0%.
Checks how full the holding's total levy (garrison + raisable) is. 1 is 100%, 0 is 0%.
Checks if a character holds a favor toward another character. The reverse condition is owes_favor_to .
Checks if a title or a ruler's primary title is a holy order.
Checks distance to the nearest holy site of the target scope
Checks if the hospital of the province has any buildings.
Checks if a hospital has the specified building.
Checks if a hospital is currently constructing the specified building.
Checks the hospital level of a province.
Checks if the character has a trait with immortal = yes
Checks which age at which a character became immortal. Always false for mortal characters
Checks how long a character has been imprisoned.
Checks if ruler is independent and not in revolt
Checks a character's personal intrigue attribute against another character or a fixed integer value. Also see realm_intrigue .
Checks if a character is currently involved in a battle.

Checks if scoped character is in a coalition against of the target character or ruler of target title/province. Province scopes must be relative (ROOT/FROM) or saved event targets, since numbers are interpreted as character IDs.
Checks if a character is leading troops.
Checks if a character is in a/no/specific faction.
Checks if a character holds any revolt title(?)
Checks if scoped character has in_seclusion character modifier.
Checks if a character is currently involved in a siege.
Check if the character is interested in the target society.
(2.8) Check if the character is interested in the society that the target character is a member of.
Checks if a character's host and employer are different characters. Note that courtiers cannot be abroad - their host is always their liege.
Checks if a wonder or wonder upgrade's active-trigger is met.
Checks if the character is an adult as set in defines on a per gender basis ( AGE_OF_ADULTHOOD_MALE and AGE_OF_ADULTHOOD_FEMALE ) - vanilla has both set at 16.
Checks if a character is alive. Also see is_dying .
Checks for alliances and tributary relationships. Does not check for being temporary war allies. Expensive calculation, use with care [3]
Checks if holding type is allowed by the government of specified character. Uses de jure capital for titles above count-tier, uses county capital holding for titles above baron-tier.
Checks if the world is randomised or shattered. Also see is_random_world and is_shattered_world
(2.8) Checks if the scoped character is a progenitor of the target character's bloodline, within up to sixteen generations (for performance reasons). Expensive, so use with caution.

Checks if the scoped artifact is currently active, as defined by its active trigger. Artifacts without an active trigger will always be considered active, even if not owned, and artifacts with an active trigger and without an owner will never be considered active.
Checks if the scoped artifact is currently equipped by its owner.

Checks if the scoped artifact is the same type as the given artifact Warning: Does not work in all contexts. In particular, this condition does NOT work in limit clauses for any_ and random_ scopes. If you want to do something to an artifact which is the same type as another artifact, expand on the example to the right: pick a pair of artifacts; add different flags to each; check if the two flagged artifacts are of the same type (see example); if they are, then you can act on the artifact with the second flag; repeat the process with different pairs of artifacts until all possible pairs have been evaluated.
Checks if the wonder is at a stage satisfies the comparison to define MIN_LOOTABLE_STAGE .
Cheecks if the wonder has fully constructed its final stage.
Checks if a character is located on an ocean province.
Checks if a combat flank or sieging army is attacking or defending.
(2.8) Checks if the current scoped character is the sibling of either of the target character's parents (i.e., one of the target character's parents' siblings, colloquially known as "piblings" ).
Checks if the wonder is currently being looted
Checks if the wonder is currently being restored
Checks if character is betrothed to anyone.
Checks if the character is the founder of the target bloodline
Checks if the character is a member of the target bloodline
Checks if a holding is constructing a new building. With "yes", checks for any new building. "no" does not work.
Checks if a province/character is currently building a tier/stage of a wonder. Can check particular wonders as well. Only true if construction is not paused.
Checks if a wonder is currently constructing an upgrade. Can check particular wonder upgrades as well. Only true if construction is not paused.
bool (in province/title scope) province/title (in character scope)

In province/title (barony) scope, checks if it's the capital of the province respectively its owner, in character scope, checks if the target scope is the character's capital. Note that the generated tooltip won't reflect the target scope, use a custom tooltip for that.

is_capital = yes
is_capital = c_parma
is_capital = 333 # Roma
Checks if the scope is a child of another character

Checks if the scope is a close relative of another character. This includes parents, children, siblings, grandparents, grandchildren, uncles, aunts, nephews, nieces, and spouse. If the character has parents, it also includes the character themself. NOTE: is_close_relative includes uncles, aunts, and spouse; any_close_relative does not.
Checks if a title has a conquest_culture flag set.

Checks if current scope matches the potential/allow block of the given decision/law/government. is_decision_potential takes a normal,  plot or society decision. is_targeted_decision_potential takes any scope to a character, province or title. is_title_decision_potential takes any scope to a title or province, except saved event target provinces. is_settlement_decision_potential takes any scope to a barony title. is_fort/hospital/trade_post_decision_potential takes any scope to a title or province. Uses province for barony or county tier titles, de jure capital for higher tier titles.

Checks if two provinces are connected via some realm's territory. Can be somewhat performance intensive, so use sparingly. Parameter Type Description target capital/ realm_capital/ scope Required. What province to find a connection to. Alternatively takes a scope that can be resolved to a province. sea_gap bool Whether to allow pathing through gaps of a single sea province. Defaults to "no". Can't path through lakes. land_gap bool Whether to allow pathing through gaps of a single land province. Defaults to "no". Can't path through wastelands. sub_realm bool/scope Which realm to allow pathing through. "yes" for the sub-realm of the province owner. "no" for the realm of the top-liege. Alternatively takes a scope that can be resolved to a character. Defaults to "yes". naval_distance bool/int Whether to allow pathing by sea (any number of provinces). Can take a number instead to use a max distance from already found ports.

content.text: Warning: Does not work in all contexts. In particular, this condition does NOT work in limit clauses for any_ and random_ scopes. If you want to do something to an artifact which is the same type as another artifact, expand on the example to the right: pick a pair of artifacts; add different flags to each; check if the two flagged artifacts are of the same type (see example); if they are, then you can act on the artifact with the second flag; repeat the process with different pairs of artifacts until all possible pairs have been evaluated.

is_decision_potential takes a normal,  plot or society decision. is_targeted_decision_potential takes any scope to a character, province or title. is_title_decision_potential takes any scope to a title or province, except saved event target provinces. is_settlement_decision_potential takes any scope to a barony title. is_fort/hospital/trade_post_decision_potential takes any scope to a title or province. Uses province for barony or county tier titles, de jure capital for higher tier titles.

Note: is_heir erroneously returns false for certain types of non-dynastic succession. Eg: If a feudal vassal has no heir, their titles will be inherited by their liege, but their liege will have is_heir = no (unless they are due to inherit another title normally).
Note: is_interested_in_any_society = no erroneously returns the exact same result as = yes . Instead, use = yes and wrap the whole thing in a NOT clause.
To check whether a title currently exists, use has_holder = yes instead.

as_if_liege = yes also applies the liege-vassal opinion modifiers ( vassal_opinion , etc.) and is used in factions, to decide if a character would like someone better as their liege than another one (and therefore would join a faction seeking to replace him).

"Troop strength" is defined to be the "Total Levy" value as per the realm structure window. [5] In practice, this "Total Levy" is approximately equal to Max Demesne Levy + Max Vassal Levy + Hired Troops + Retinues + Special Event Troops. IE: Depletion of levies (due to sieges, battles, etc) has no impact on relative_power .
- Values: BARON, COUNT, DUKE, KING, EMPEROR
